lawyer: Md. Ahsanul Kabir with Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocates ----- For the Plaintiff Petitioner
parties:
Captain Md. Mobarak Hossain, Master, ATM Dolores ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
vs 
MT Dolores and others Defendants ------ Defendants Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff submits that defendant No. 1 vessel has no assets in Bangladesh. The plaintiff submits that the principal defendant opposite parties are now making preparation to beach and scrap the defendant No. 1 opposite party vessel MT Dolores by transferring the same to a third party which is now lying at Jetty No. 10 of Chittagong Port. The said defendant No. 1 vessel MT Dolores may leave the territorial waters of Bangladesh at any time. He has submitted that the principal defendant opposite parties have no other moveable and immoveable properties in Bangladesh. He submits that if the vessel is not arrested the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss and injury inasmuch as there will be no other way to satisfy the decree that may be passed in course of hearing of the suit. It appears from materials placed in support of his contention that he was appointed as master of the vessel on 28.3.94. The owners of the vessel informed the shipping master on 30.3.94 that the plaintiff petitioner had failed to join the vessel and so they had arranged to sign on one Captain Shah Alam in the ship's article. He further informed the Shipping Master to sign off the plaintiff from the article. The shipping master in turn by a letter dated 11.6.94 informed the plaintiff petitioner of the contention of the owners. There is nothing on record to show that the plaintiff controverted the allegation of the owners of the vessel nor any document to show that he actually worked as the Master except that his name was entered in the article on 28.3.94 which the owners of the vessel had requested the Shipping Master to be signed off. The plaintiff had remained silent from the receipt of the Shipping Master's letter written to him on 11.6.94.
